subject: Skyfoundry dedicated footprint / traffic vignette
messages:
From: Anika Singh <anika@skyfoundry.ai>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-12T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated sizing — initial traffic snapshot

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the quick intro call this morning. As discussed, we'd like Redwood to size a dedicated GPU footprint for our LLM features (semantic search + chat assistance) ahead of our Q4 launch. Attaching a small sample of real traffic profiles and a token mix PDF — hopefully enough to start a rough sizing.

High-level:
- Peak concurrent sessions: ~220 (observed over a 3h window during our beta)
- Typical prompt length: 40–120 tokens; responses average 150–450 tokens (varies by user intent)
- Mix: ~65% chat (stateful sessions), 25% single-shot embeddings, 10% rerank/administrative ops
- SLA target: 99.9% availability, p99 latency for streaming chat <= 650ms

Could you confirm what additional telemetry you need to turn this into a Dedicated proposal (GPU SKUs, burst allowances, fallback model recommendations)? Also please confirm an estimated timeline for a pilot.

Thanks — Anika
Anika Singh, Head of ML Systems
Skyfoundry

Attachments: skyfoundry_sample_traffic.csv (text/csv), token_mix_snapshot.pdf (application/pdf)

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: Anika Singh <anika@skyfoundry.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-12T13:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing — initial traffic snapshot

Hi Anika — great to meet you earlier. I pulled your sample and sketched a first-pass set of questions so our sizing is aligned with real load characteristics. Can you paste answers inline below or drop a short reply with the CSV column definitions? Once we have these, Karthik and Ben will help finalize GPU SKU mapping and pricing. Proposed next steps: 48h intake -> pilot sizing -> pilot kickoff (2–3 week runway).

Questions (short):
1) Concurrency granularity: is your "220 concurrent sessions" measured as long-lived interactive sessions (avg session duration) or short-lived requests aggregated? If long-lived, what's the average session lifetime (minutes)?
2) Request arrival shape: do you see sharp spikes (10–15x baseline) during product events, or mostly smooth daily rhythms with 2–3x peaks?
3) Streaming behavior: what fraction of chat requests use streaming API vs non-streaming responses?
4) KV/prefix cache applicability: do chat sessions reuse prior conversation state frequently (prefix hits)? If so, approximate prefix hit rate (0–1).
5) Embedding workload: batch sizes you use, average dimensions, and target latency for embedding calls?
6) Failure & fallback policy: would you prefer automatic fallback to smaller/quantized variants during burst / or deny traffic?

Also forwarding your CSV + tokens to Karthik for a quick occupancy sketch.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Onboarding checklist attached: skyfoundry_sample_traffic.csv (we referenced)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-13T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing — initial traffic snapshot

Kim — quick internal note after scanning their sample. Observations and immediate asks for the customer before we size: 
- Token mix indicates median response ~240 tokens but 95th at ~820 tokens — significant tail. Need clarification on whether 95th is a product edge-case or user-facing burst.
- If sessions are long-lived with high prefix reuse (>0.6), KVCaching will cut per-token cost and reduce memory pressure; ask them to confirm.
- For the 220 concurrent sessions: if these are active streaming sessions, GPU memory per session matters (KV cache + activations). If they are mostly quick single-shot interactions, throughput is the dominant constraint.

Preliminary SKU recommendation (rough):
- Start pilot on 4x A800/80GB (or equivalent) nodes with 1:1 model placement for a medium-sized Llama2-Chat variant (quantized FP8/INT8 option) for latency-sensitive chat.
- Add 2x T4-style cheaper machines for embedding batching if their embedding latency tolerance is >200ms.

Questions for the intake email to the customer (I'll draft):
- Confirm session lifetime and streaming ratio
- Provide 1 week of minute-level arrival rate samples around peak events
- Confirm embedding batch sizes and SLOs

Ben — can you note any commercial constraints (minimum pilot term, burst buffer policy) so we can include in the reply?

—Karthik

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-13T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing — initial traffic snapshot

Looping in commercial constraints:
- Pilot: 4–6 week pilot with month-to-month afterwards is typical. We can do a 30% pilot discount on committed nodes if they convert to a 12mo reserved capacity.
- Burst buffer: standard policy is 20% free burst for first 30 days post-provisioning, then discretionary expansion subject to capacity. We can include a contractual burst allowance for their launch window if needed (requires pricing uplift).
- SLA exceptions: 99.9% is achievable on Dedicated; any stronger SLA or financial credits will need infra carve-outs and a higher commitment.

I'll add those bullets into the reply draft.

—Ben

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: Anika Singh <anika@skyfoundry.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-16T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing — initial traffic snapshot

Anika — thanks for the sample. Below is our intake checklist to get from you; if easier we can hop on a 30m call to run through. Once we have these items we'll lock the pilot SKU mix and send a scoped proposal.

Skyfoundry Dedicated Intake Checklist (please reply inline):
1) Concurrency detail: Are the ~220 concurrent sessions long-lived (minutes+) or short requests? If long-lived, please provide average & 95th session lifetime.
2) Streaming ratio: percent of chat requests using streaming vs full-response (estimates okay).
3) Arrival shape: minute-level arrival rate for your biggest observed peak (CSV preferred) or a 1-hour high-resolution window.
4) Token distributions: confirm median/95th for prompt and response (we saw median prompt ~70, median response ~240, response 95th ~820).
5) Prefix reuse / KV cache: estimated prefix hit rate (0.0–1.0) and typical retained window (messages).
6) Embedding details: batch size, model dims, target p50/p95 latency.
7) Acceptable fallback: do you want automatic fallback to quantized model variants during extreme bursts, or prefer to throttle?
8) Compliance note: confirm whether logs/requests must remain in a private VPC or if hosted Dedicated with audit logs is acceptable.

Pilot proposal (scratch):
- Initial pilot: 4x A800-equivalent nodes for chat (quantized model); 2x cheaper nodes for embedding batching. Estimated sustainable concurrency (interactive sessions) ~180 with p99 streaming latency ~550–700ms depending on prefix reuse.
- Burst plan: 20% free burst for first 30 days; contractual burst available for launch (pricing uplift).
- Commercial: pilot 4–6 weeks; 30% pilot-to-reservation conversion credit for 12mo commit (Ben to include terms).

If you'd like a call, I'm available Wed or Thu afternoon PT.

Thanks — looking forward to the details.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0128
